title: Oracle May Truck Gas to New Mexico AI Site at Four Times Pipeline Cost
summary:
Oracle is exploring deliveries of compressed natural gas by truck to bring the early stages of its 2.45 GW Project Jupiter AI data center in New Mexico online before a delayed pipeline enters service, Bloomberg reported. The campus is part of the Stargate buildout for OpenAI and will use Bloom Energy fuel cells for power.

Oracle already uses truck deliveries at data centers in Utah and Texas. The approach kept a site outside Salt Lake City moving forward for more than a year while it awaited a pipeline, but trucked gas costs roughly four times as much as pipeline deliveries.

Project Jupiter has faced a six month delay to a key gas pipeline, and its $18 billion in construction debt was recently quoted around 84 cents on the dollar. Oracle sent the developer, a Blue Owl unit, a force majeure notice seeking to defer payments if the campus misses its planned 2028 opening, rather than withdraw as tenant. Oracle said, “Project Jupiter remains on our planned schedule.”

ORACLE SEEKS PROTECTION FROM DATA CENTER DELAYS

$ORCL has issued a force majeure notice tied to Project Jupiter, the 2.45GW New Mexico data center that is part of the Stargate AI buildout, Bloomberg reports.

Oracle is not trying to exit the project, but is seeking to delay payments if the site misses its planned 2028 opening.

The project has faced permitting setbacks, including a six-month delay to a key gas pipeline. Its $18B construction debt is already trading below 90 cents on the dollar.

Oracle says the project remains on schedule.

selectedTweets.text:
🦔Oracle sent a force majeure notice on Project Jupiter, its AI data center in New Mexico built for the $400 billion Stargate deal with OpenAI. The campus needs a 17-mile gas pipeline to power its Bloom Energy fuel cells. New Mexico denied the pipeline permits twice. Oracle wants the right to delay payments if the site misses its 2028 opening. $18 billion in project loans are at 89 to 91 cents on the dollar. ORCL fell 5%.

My Take
Force majeure is for earthquakes and wars. Oracle filed one over a gas permit they got denied twice. A company with $167 billion in debt and a junk-adjacent credit rating just told its development partner it might not pay on time. I think Oracle's balance sheet is worse than the market has priced in, and this notice is the first public admission.

Twenty banks lent $18 billion for this project and they can't move the debt. Santander and Jefferies are stuck with more than they planned to hold. That loan assumed Oracle's backlog converts to revenue on schedule, but half the backlog is OpenAI, a company that burns cash faster than it earns it. SemiAnalysis has first power at this site in 2029. The banks underwrote 2028. I think the AI infrastructure bet cracks here first, in the loan market, before it ever shows up in stock prices, and the banks who funded the construction are the ones left with the bill.

Hedgie🤗

selectedTweets.quotedTweetText:
PROJECT JUPITER  .. Data Center Pain

The loan is private so some guestimating on my part.

The loan is a construction loan with a term of 4 years w/ up to 2, 1 year extensions paying S +250 bps. 

Ultimately, the asset backing the loan is a long term lease of the data center in New Mexico to Oracle. 

The delay due to power is not the only issue. 

10 year rates are 100 bps higher and ORCL credit spreads are 100 wider since the issuance of the loan in December '25. 

So 200 bps increase on a 15 to 18 year annuity (lease) payment is worth about 15 pts depending on discount rates. 

While max maturity of this loan is 6 years, the asset backing the loan (lease to ORCL) is much longer duration. 

My guess is that Blue Owl contributed about 10-15 pts of equity. 

So their equity is worth less (unless they hedged rates and credit).

Before the recent news of power permitting delays, the loans were trading 90ish.

Now ORCL may have the ability to make lower payment until DC is operating which makes the asset value of the lease less. 

Hearing next trade could be around 80. 

20 point markdown in 9 months on a loan that was marketed as "cheap" ORCL risk.

selectedTweets.text:
The $ORCL delay is, I'm afraid, a permitting story. Water rights, a gas pipeline, and a state writing its data center rules in real time. 

All public for weeks- @RegardingDC has had the timeline the whole way.
selectedTweets.quotedTweetText:
Oracle is preparing for the possibility of delays outside its control. Nothing more.

Last week, Democratic gubernatorial nominee Deb Haaland said that she would immediately pause new large-scale data center proposals while lawmakers write statewide rules for the industry. Polymarket has her at a 95% chance of winning office.

Project Jupiter was allowed to drill a new well before a formal public hearing, using an emergency exception. This bypassed the formal public hearing process, which community members were upset about.

The New Mexico Supreme Court temporarily halted proceedings tied to the project’s emergency water well after legal challenges. The court later rejected those challenges and allowed the permitting process to resume at the beginning of September.

Last week, Doña Ana County created a Community Monitoring Committee specifically for Project Jupiter. The county resolution cites continued concerns from residents over water, air, noise, pollution, and other environmental impacts, and calls for independent public information forums around the project, putting the project under a microscope.

At Tuesday’s county meeting (9/22), the Mesilla Valley Economic Development Alliance presented the scale of Project Jupiter’s expected impact: 750 announced jobs, $50 billion in Phase 1 investment, and more than 2 million square feet of facilities, trying to remind the county how beneficial the project is for them.

$ORCL is moving forward with Project Jupiter while the project is simultaneously going through permitting scrutiny, local monitoring, and a broader statewide debate over how New Mexico should regulate large data centers. I, too, would want to defer debt for things outside of my control.

We have this whole timeline at https://t.co/1i4c3TmQ4O.

Potentially key assist for $ORCL’s massive New Mexico "Project Jupiter" data center, the subject of last week's Force Majeure filing: retired federal judge James Browning, a George W. Bush appointee, tapped to oversee the contentious air-permit proceeding after the prior hearing officer recused.

Energy Transfer ($ET) has proposed rerouting the gas pipeline around state land after activist Democratic Land Commissioner Stephanie Garcia Richard twice blocked the original route.

Lots of delays, lots of workarounds. But with up to $165B of possible investment over 30 years, also lots of incentive to work through the obstacles.
